correctness.rationale: The normalized density follows by differentiating the CDF. The exact identity \(2[x(1-x)]^2\frac{d^2}{dx^2}\log f=(\tau\tanh(\tau s-a)-\tanh s)^2-(\tau^2-1)\) is checked symbolically. Evaluating at the midpoint yields the necessary condition \(|a|\le\operatorname{arcosh}\tau\). Sufficiency holds for every real \(s\): the auxiliary inverse-hyperbolic function comparing the extreme biases \(a=\pm\operatorname{arcosh}\tau\) has derivative with the sign of \(\tanh s\), hence a global minimum at zero. The argument covers all boundaries and \(0<\tau<1\) strictly log-convex, plus the uniform case. Exact derivatives and 76 finite rational signs were reproduced; no finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact necessary-and-sufficient alpha-temperature boundary is a substantive density-shape classification, not simply a counterexample or renaming of an old distribution. It resolves a real imprecision in a published high-temperature statement, quantifies how the minimum log-concavity temperature blows up as Bernoulli class probability approaches zero or one, and supplies a global sufficiency argument for all x. This naturally informs when a Concrete relaxation can be used in log-concave density computations, without claiming guarantees for multivariate relaxations.
